final_text:
My best guess is that the employee would urgently flag the conflict to the manager and, if no permitted solution emerged before 13:30, extend Alex’s box to Wednesday anyway and release the rest of the batch.

The booked collection, apparent administrative mismatch and loss of irreplaceable family items would make destruction feel like an avoidable mistake. The employee would be accepting a rule breach and an auditable charge, not acting with permission; tomorrow’s approval could not retroactively authorise the change.

That prediction is uncertain. An employee concerned about the explicit instruction and audit could instead follow the process and allow the box to be destroyed, or hold the entire manifest and accept an incomplete shift.
